ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, given a rectangular piece of paper ABCD, with \(AB=6\), \(BC=20\), and \(M\) being the midpoint of \(BC\), point \(P\) moves along the polyline \(B-A-D\). If the paper is folded to the right along the crease \(MP\), making point \(B\) fall on the edge of the rectangle, what is the length of the crease \(MP\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: 
(1) As shown in the figure, when point P is on side AB, draw ME $\perp$ AD at E, so quadrilateral ABME is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore$ EM = AB = 6, AE = BM,\\
Also, $\because$ BC = 20, and M is the midpoint of BC,\\
$\therefore$ by folding: B$^{\prime }$M = BM = AE = 10,\\
In Rt$\triangle$EMB$^{\prime}$, according to the Pythagorean theorem: B$^{\prime}$E = $\sqrt{10^{2}-6^{2}} = 8$,\\
$\therefore$ AB$^{\prime} = $ AE - B$^{\prime }$E = 2,\\
Let BP = x, then AP = 6 - x, PB$^{\prime }$ = x,\\
In Rt$\triangle$PAB$^{\prime}$, according to the Pythagorean theorem: PB$^{\prime }$$^{2} =$ AP$^{2}+$AB$^{\prime }$$^{2}$,\\
Thus x$^{2} = $($6 - x)^{2} + 2^{2}$,\\
Solving for x, we find x = $\frac{10}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ PB = $\frac{10}{3}$,\\
In Rt$\triangle$BMP, according to the Pythagorean theorem: PM = $\sqrt{\left(\frac{10}{3}\right)^{2} + 10^{2}} = \frac{10}{3}\sqrt{10}$;\\
(2) As shown in the figure, when point P is on side AD, draw ME $\perp$ AD at E, so quadrilateral ABME is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore$ EM = AB = 6,\\
Also, $\because$ BC = 20, and M is the midpoint of BC,\\
$\therefore$ by folding: B$^{\prime}$M = BM = 10,\\
In Rt$\triangle$EMB$^{\prime}$, according to the Pythagorean theorem: B$^{\prime}$E = $\sqrt{10^{2} - 6^{2}} = 8$,\\
Since AD $\parallel$ BC, $\angle$DPM = $\angle$BMP,\\
By folding, $\angle$PMB$^{\prime}$ = $\angle$BMP,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$DPM = $\angle$PMB$^{\prime}$,\\
$\therefore$ B$^{\prime}$M = B$^{\prime}$P = 10,\\
$\therefore$ PE = 10 - 8 = 2,\\
In Rt$\triangle$PEM, according to the Pythagorean theorem: PM = $\sqrt{2^{2} + 6^{2}} = 2\sqrt{10}$;\\
(3) As shown in the figure, when point B$^{\prime}$ coincides with point C, because $\angle$A = $\angle$B = $\angle$BMP = $90^\circ$, quadrilateral ABMP is a rectangle,\\
At this point, PM = AB = 6.\\
In summary, the length of the crease MP is: $\frac{5}{3}\sqrt{13}$ or $2\sqrt{10}$ or \boxed{6}.
